item.title: Can the U.S. and Iran take the off-ramp?
item.description: The U.S. military has paused its airstrikes on Iran after nearly two weeks of intensifying bombing, while diplomatic efforts have pushed forward to try to avert a return to all-out war.

item.title: With just a few primary elections to go, the competitive Senate map keeps shifting
item.description: For Democrats to take control of the U.S. Senate, they have to flip 4 seats currently held by Republicans. Republicans, meanwhile, are playing defense and pickup opportunities are harder to find.

item.description: The route for the iconic cycling race's final stage was shortened because security and police were reassigned to assist with wildfires in southwest France.

item.title: U.S. pauses attacks on Iran for a second straight day and Tehran does too
item.description: The United States paused attacks on Iran for a second straight day Sunday and Tehran said it had done so too, as efforts continued to bring the countries back to negotiations on an interim ceasefire.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Rage-giving, innovation and cuts: How public media has survived without federal funds
item.description: A year after President Trump signed a law ending six decades of federal funding of public media, it's a time of reinvention, innovation and clear anxiety at public tv and radio stations nationwide.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Lebanese displaced by war turn to satellites to check their homes
item.description: Unable to return home, some Lebanese displaced by Israel's invasion of southern Lebanon are buying satellite images to see whether their houses survived.

item.title: ADHD looks different in women and poses unique health risks
item.description: For decades, ADHD was viewed as a childhood condition that mostly affected boys. Researchers now know ADHD manifests differently in girls, but many still go undiagnosed until adulthood.

item.title: Meet the robots programmed by kids to speak their Indigenous languages
item.description: Many Native American languages are endangered. With the help of his mentor, a 12-year-old in Michigan hopes to help preserve his language through robotics.

item.title: Climate change is now threatening a pillar of childhood: summer break
item.description: When summer rolls around, many parents scramble to sign up their young kids for outdoor activities. But what do you do when extreme heat and wildfire smoke increasingly make the outdoors dangerous?

item.title: Suspect in Berlin Pride vehicle attack is dead, police say
item.description: Germany's interior minister Alexander Dobrindt described the incident as a likely "Islamic terror attack," and named the suspect as Abdul Ballout, who was born in Germany and has Lebanese roots.
